title: Prometheus + TraceFusion experiment logbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is an experiment logbook for a lightweight integration we’re calling "TraceFusion" — an operational pattern to directly correlate Prometheus metrics with reconstructed OpenTelemetry traces for LLM inference paths. The goal: make metric->trace navigation seamless for operators while keeping Prom scrape volume bounded and trace sampling cost predictable.

Scope and constraints (quick):
- Focus: tokenized inference paths, KV-cache effects, prefix-warmth probes, and tail-latency outliers for multi-tenant hosted API.
- Non-goal: full-fidelity end-to-end distributed traces for every request (too expensive). We want representative fused artifacts to speed triage.
- Budget: target incremental trace storage < 15% of current trace costs; query-cost budget for dashboards < $400/month per 10k QPS team (ballpark).

Hypotheses to test:
H1: A small set (~5) of Prometheus-derived probes (quantile, tail rate, kv-warmth ratio) can be used to trigger on-demand short-lived trace capture windows that contain relevant spans for debugging high-latency tokens.
H2: Merging probe metadata into trace spans (trace labels) will reduce operator time-to-root-cause by at least 30% in synthetic incident drills.
H3: Lightweight trace fusion (attach metric snapshot to the sampled spans) produces actionable telemetry without blowing storage budget if sampling is severity-weighted.

Experiment design (steps):
1) Instrument a probe layer (probe-exporter) that queries Prometheus rules and emits sampled trace triggers to the agent.
   - Probe definitions are PromQL rules evaluating rolling 1m/5m windows.
   - Probe exporter exposes a control plane endpoint to request a 10s trace window for matching nodes/pods.
2) Modify OTEL collector config to accept "trace-trigger" events which cause short-term sampling rate increase bounded by label selectors (tenant_id, model_family, path_hash).
3) For fused artifacts, collector will attach the latest matching Prometheus probe snapshot (key metrics and tags) as span attributes on the root span for the window.
4) Dashboard changes: add a "TraceFusion Scopes" panel grouping probe events that resulted in traces with links to trace IDs and embedded metric snapshot.
5) Run synthetic incident drills (see test matrix below) and measure triage time and signal fidelity.

Probe catalog (initial):
- probe_kv_warmth_drop: PromQL: rate(kv_warmth_fraction{job=~"inference.*"}[1m]) < 0.05
  - rationale: KV warm fraction is a leading indicator for cold-cache tails.
- probe_token_tail_latency: PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le, model, pod)) > 0.5
  - rationale: spikes in 99th token latency.
- probe_prefix_eviction_rate: PromQL: increase(prefix_evictions_total[5m]) > 10
  - rationale: frequent prefix eviction correlates with ineffective caching.
- probe_batched_queue_length: PromQL: avg_over_time(batcher_queue_length[1m]) > 20
  - rationale: high queueing leads to throughput-latency tradeoffs.
- probe_multi_model_fanout: PromQL: sum(rate(routing_fanout_total[1m])) by (pod) / sum(rate(requests_total[1m])) by (pod) > 2.5
  - rationale: unexpected fanout elevates tail work.

Trace capture rules (policy draft):
- On trigger, increase sampling to 50% for 10s for the matching pod(s) and attach probe_id and probe_snapshot to trace root span.
- Severity-weighting: if probe value > emergency threshold (defined per probe), escalate to 100% for 30s and tag sample as high-priority.
- Per-tenant cap: no more than N traces per tenant per hour (configurable).
- Fallback: if trace storage nearing budget, reduce non-priority trace retention to 7 days and compress spans (strip verbose attributes).

Collector/Agent changes (notes to eng):
- OTEL collector: add custom receiver for "probe-trigger" events (small REST webhook) that updates in-memory sampling policy TTLs. Keep it simple and stateless beyond TTL map.
- Agent on inference nodes: expose a secure endpoint to start a short-term capture (collect stack spans, small tags, no raw payloads). Need strict PII rules — do not include prompt content in spans. Use prompt-hash and length only.
- Security: events should be signed with service account and verified by collector.

Dashboard wireframe (investigation flow):
1) Top row: probe heatmap (by cluster, region) showing active probes over time. Click a cell = drill modal with last 10 triggers.
2) Middle row: probe snapshot carousel: shows metric snapshot (key series), top correlated spans (latency by span), tenant distribution.
3) Bottom row: quicklinks -> traces (in trace UI), sample trace view with attached metric snapshot, action buttons (create Jira, annotate incident, add to watchlist).
4) New UX: "metric->trace" keyboard shortcut that opens the nearest trace for the selected metric point (needs backend index mapping).

Sample queries (PromQL) to copy into exporter config: 
- kv_warmth_ratio: avg_over_time(kv_warmth_fraction{pod=~"$pod"}[30s])
- tail_latency_rate: increase(token_latency_count{le="+Inf",pod=~"$pod"}[1m]) - increase(token_latency_count{le="0.2",pod=~"$pod"}[1m])

Metrics to attach to root span (snapshot fields):
- probe_id, probe_value, probe_threshold, model_family, tenant_id (hashed), pod, region, recent_errors_count, kv_warmth_fraction, 1m_p50_token_latency, 1m_p95_token_latency, 1m_p99_token_latency, batcher_queue_len_avg

Acceptance criteria (for roll-out to canary):
- Operators can reliably navigate from metric spike -> trace in < 20s (manual test).
- Synthetic drills: mean triage time reduced by 30% vs baseline (3 runs per scenario).
- Storage budgets: incremental trace storage < 15% and query cost within forecast for 2 weeks of traffic.

Test matrix (short):
- Scenarios: cold-cache tail, sudden fanout, noisy tenant flood, batcher overload, intermittent prefix evictions.
- Variables: model size (small/medium/large), tenant isolation (high/low), region (us-west/us-east/eur).
- Metrics collected: triage time, traces captured per trigger, probe false-positive rate, operator usefulness score (survey).

Open questions / risks:
- Data privacy: attaching metric snapshots may still risk inference of prompt characteristics. Use strong hashing and retention rules.
- Indexing: need an index service to map metric timestamp -> trace ID quickly. How do we handle clock skew? Consider monotonic sequence numbers emitted with triggers.
- Cost control: worst-case correlated probes could trigger excessive traces. Need safety valves (global rate limiter + per-team budgets).
- Observability chicken-and-egg: probe exporter itself needs telemetry. Keep it minimal and instrumented with its own SLI.

Next steps (concrete):
- Priya: carve a tiny prototype exporter (Python) to evaluate PromQL -> webhook flow (ETA 1 week).
- Liam: spike OTEL receiver and sampling TTL map (ETA 1.5 weeks).
- Ava: dashboard mock (Figma + panel queries) and sprintly usability test plan (ETA 2 weeks).
- Ethan: cost model estimate (storage + query) based on current trace retention and 1% increased sampling scenarios (ETA 1 week).
- Sync: set up weekly 30m runbook review and one tabletop drill at end of spike (2025-03-07).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep default probe sensitivity conservative to avoid noise -> traces (we've seen old 'token tail' rules trigger too often).
- If this works, long-term: consider a "trace-mini-replay" feature that replays minimal context with metric aggregate for offline deep-dive.
- Make sure product folks sign off on tenant-level sampling and customer-visible telemetry choices before canary.

Log entries (experiment timeline):
- 2025-02-14: initial doc + hypothesis capture (Priya)
- 2025-02-17: prototype exporter began (Priya) — wiring PromQL -> webhook, low-volume test on staging cluster.
- 2025-02-20: OTEL sampling TTL POC (Liam) — TTL map applied, traces captured for 10s windows in staging.
- 2025-02-24: first dashboard mock (Ava) — added probe heatmap and trace links in Grafana; working on trace snapshot panel.
- 2025-02-28: cost model first pass (Ethan) — estimated +9% trace storage for 25% peek sampling; need throttles.

Appendix: related tickets and bookmarks:
- OBS-421: tracefusion spike; owner: Priya
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/138 (prototype probe-exporter)
- Confluence: tracefusion-overview (design notes and privacy checklist)

Comments / TODOs for reviewers:
- Please check the probe thresholds above — these are intentionally conservative baselines.
- Feedback needed on privacy constraints (what to redact) and whether we can include prompt-length histogram as attribute.

End of logbook entry.
